# Coding 0.6.3

This release adds first-class OpenAI Responses API support to the Go SDK and
improves how Coding presents reasoning summaries and streaming tool input.

## Highlights

- OpenAI models can now use the Responses API alongside the existing Chat
  Completions adapter. Responses preserve provider response IDs, output phases,
  token usage, reasoning summaries, and function calls through the shared
  `llm` API.
- Strict function tools are supported explicitly. Tool schemas can request
  constrained arguments, while streamed argument fragments remain available to
  callers as they arrive.
- Stateless Responses conversations can replay encrypted reasoning together
  with assistant output and tool results when the provider returns the required
  reasoning items.
- Coding now carries streamed tool arguments through the service and displays
  them while a tool call is being prepared. Model-provided bold reasoning
  headings become compact titles for collapsible thinking details.

## SDK and model compatibility

- The OpenAI adapter is organized into separate Chat Completions and Responses
  implementations with shared transport and protocol utilities. Existing Chat
  Completions compatibility behavior remains available.
- Responses streaming uses the official typed event and output unions from
  `openai-go`, including text, reasoning, function arguments, refusals, usage,
  and terminal outcomes.
- The generated model catalog has been refreshed with current provider routes
  and now exposes supported OpenAI Responses models from OpenCode sources.
- `github.com/openai/openai-go/v3` has been updated to 3.48.0.

## Streaming behavior

SSE event size and frequency are controlled by each provider. A compatible
endpoint may return an entire text response or function argument object in one
delta, and some routes do not expose reasoning summaries or encrypted reasoning
even when those fields are requested. Coding preserves the events it receives
without manufacturing artificial chunks.

## Downloads and current limitations

DMG and ZIP builds are available for Apple Silicon (`arm64`) and Intel (`x64`)
Macs running macOS 12 or later. Windows and Linux builds are not included.

The macOS builds are ad-hoc signed, but are not signed with an Apple Developer
ID certificate and are not notarized. macOS may require approval under
**System Settings > Privacy & Security** after the first launch attempt.

The embedded browser should currently be used only with content you trust.
Dedicated isolation for untrusted pages is not complete.
